scope: Theorem 4.2 (Multiplicity estimate of Moura) of the manuscript “One Rational Matrix Hitting Point for Noncommutative Formulas” (preprints/One-Rational-Matrix-Hitting-Point-for-Noncommutative-Formulas-September-24-2026/One-Rational-Matrix-Hitting-Point-for-Noncommutative-Formulas-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 116 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 984d0d4287bc29fc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let F be a field of characteristic zero, and let n, m ≥ 1. Suppose that q ∈ F[z] has degree n and q(0) ̸= 0, that P ∈ Matm(F[z]) has entries of degree at most n − 1, and that G ∈ GLm(F[[z]]), G′ = (P/q)G. For a constant row u ∈ F1×m and a constant column v ∈ Fm×1, if y = uGv is nonzero, then ord0 y ≤ (n − 1) m 2 ! + m − 1. (11)
